text:
Alex: heads-up — ran a load sweep on prod-dedicated last night; started seeing OOMs when we pushed batch size +20% for the long-seq workload. attaching quick notes from the profiler and a few observations.

Maria: can you paste the nsys snippets? was this during a rollout that changed kernel selection or quantization?

Alex: yeah, rollout toggled the new kernel-selector heuristic (seq-aware pick). interestingly, when selector picked kernel_v2 we saw ~12% less TFLOPS but GPU memory transiently spiked. nsys snapshot: 
```
Time  GPU_mem  Kernel
00:01  74.2GB  kernel_v2_matmul
00:02  77.8GB  kernel_v2_attn  <-- OOM window closes ~3s later
00:03  63.1GB  kernel_v1_attn
```
Looks like v2 has larger workspace requirements for long kv-cache sequences.

Ben: that matches local repro. v2 preallocates a workspace sized for max_seq rounded up to 2048 which is wasteful for most requests. If cache shards leak, combined workspace + shards pushes >device_mem.

Priya: do we have metrics on prefix-cache shard sizes and hit rates? I suspect TTL/resizing caused shard count to grow unexpectedly during the sweep.

Alex: yes — metrics from the prefix-cache exporter: 
```
prefix_cache_total_shards: 48
prefix_cache_avg_shard_bytes: 420MB
prefix_cache_hit_rate_1h: 0.62
active_kv_items: 1.9M
```
Shard count jumped from 32 -> 48 after we increased per-request model context to 4096 in the canary.

Maria: 420MB avg shard * 48 = ~20GB just for prefix shards. Add workspace ~8-10GB and model weights 12GB -> close to 40GB limit on A100-40. On 80GB devices it's fine but we have mixed pool.

Ben: root cause seems composite: new kernel_v2 workspace + increased shard sizing + batch heuristic pushing more requests into single batch. Three moving parts.

Priya: thoughts on mitigations:
- lower default shard_max_bytes to 256MB and add adaptive shrink when hit_rate < 0.7
- set kernel-selector to prefer kernel_v1 if projected_workspace + shard_budget > device_free * 0.9
- change batching heuristic to cap combined_workspace_estimate per-batch

Alex: implemented a quick PoC for adaptive shard sizing. It evicts oldest prefixes when memory budget exceeded and reduces new shard allocs by 25%. Benchmarks: drop in OOM rate from 3.2/hour -> 0.1/hour under synthetic long-tail traffic.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: alex/poc-prefix-evict -> staging (sha: a1b2c3)

Maria: nice. We should also ensure allocator fragmentation isn't making headroom inaccurate. Any pmap/cuMemGetInfo traces?

Alex: have cuMemGetInfo logs around the OOM window: 
```
free_mem_before: 9.6GB
total_mem: 80.0GB
free_mem_after_alloc: 200MB  <-- fragmentation evident
```
We saw many small allocations for temporary buffers during attn kernel init. Fragmentation + big shard blocks bad.

Ben: allocator tuning suggestions: use a per-device pooled allocator with larger bins for 16MB-256MB to reduce fragmentation. Also enable buffer reuse for KV cache registrations: keep small tensor slab per-stream to satisfy transient allocs.

Priya: agree. Also add a preflight check in the scheduler: before growing batch or selecting kernel_v2, compute estimated_peak = reserved_model_weights + estimated_shard_budget + kernel_workspace_estimate + (batch_size * per-request_workbuf). If estimated_peak > device_free - safety_margin then fallback to safer kernel or split batch.

Alex: implemented preflight check in runtime (branch in router). sample pseudo: 
```py
def preflight(device, model, batch):
    est = model.weights + model.cache_budget(batch) + model.kernel.workspace(batch) + batch.total_workbuf
    return est < device.free * 0.85
```
Using 0.85 margin prevented 95% of the previously observed OOMs in canary.

Maria: any perf regression from falling back to kernel_v1? We care about latency impact.

Alex: 95th latency increased ~6-8% for long sequences when fallback happened, but overall p99 SLO still met since fallback only used when memory tight. For many customers with smaller context, v2 still used.

Ben: for long term, we should:
- rework kernel_v2 workspace to be allocation-on-demand (lazy) instead of full prealloc; allow smaller workspace + fallback path to split attention blocks
- add shard compaction job: background evict/compact to reduce live shard bytes (TTL tuning + LRU compaction)
- instrument more fine-grained device-level accounting (track reserved vs actually used memory by workspace)

Priya: TTL policy suggestion: default TTL 30 min, but auto-shrink TTL to 5-10 min under memory pressure or when hit_rate < 0.5. Also consider tiered cache: hot prefixes pinned, cold shards persisted to cheaper backing store (disk) with async fetch to minimize memory footprint.

Alex: can we safely move cold shards to host pinned memory and page-in as needed? Concern about page-in latency for critical requests.

Ben: yes but add predictive prefetch for likely next tokens (simple n-gram predictor) for chat workloads, and use async prefetch with suspend/resume to avoid blocking fast-path. Bad cases will still pay the latency but will be fewer.

Maria: action items: 
- Ben: prototype pooled allocator bins + KV slab reuse (due EOD Fri)
- Alex: land preflight checks + adaptive shard eviction in canary (in review)
- Priya: implement TTL autoshrink policy + metrics for shard churn and host-backend paging (start Monday)
- Maria: run a cross-pool stress with mixed A100-40 and A100-80 to validate heuristics (next run Wed)

Alex: will post canary logs after deploy. TL;DR: combination of kernel workspace and prefix-shard growth caused OOMs; mitigations: preflight memory estimates, adaptive shard sizing/eviction, allocator tuning, and possible host-tiering for cold shards.

Priya: thanks — this is a great example of multivariate perf issues. small wins + one medium project (kernel lazy allocation) should stabilize. :rocket: 

Ben: +1. keep the notes here and we can convert to runbook entries for oncall.

Alex: done — created runbook PR and linked to the canary results.``
